1. Allowed, subject to all just exceptions.
2. Application stands disposed of.

The instant petition under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (Cr.P.C.) has been filed by the petitioners seeking quashing of FIR bearing no. 255/2021 registered at Police Station Dwarka North, Delhi for offences punishable under Sections 498A/406/34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (IPC) and all other proceedings emanating therefrom.
4. Issue notice.
Mr. Satish Kumar, learned APP accepts notice on behalf of the State.

5. Petitioners are present before this Court and have been identified by their counsel Mr. D.K.
Sharma and Investigating Officer (IO) W/SI Rima Raj from Police Station Dwarka North, Delhi.
6. Brief facts of the present case are that marriage between petitioner no. 1 and respondent no. 2 was solemnized on 13.06.2015.

It is stated that due to temperamental differences, parties started Sh Ravinder @ Ravinder Suhag And Ors vs The State Govt Of Nct Of Delhi & Ors on 21 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92345588/

sentences.text: On 15.01.2021, respondent no. 2 filed a maintenance case under Section 125 of Cr.P.C. against petitioner no. 1 before Family Court, Dwarka Courts, Delhi and the same has been withdrawn on 28.11.2022.
On 16.01.2021, respondent no. 2 filed a complaint under Section 12 of DV Act against petitioners.

On 24.04.2021, respondent no. 2 filed a complaint against the petitioners before CAW Cell and on which the present FIR bearing no. 255/2021 for the offences punishable under Section 498A/406/34 IPC was registered at Police Station Dwarka North, Delhi against petitioners.

With the intervention of elders and friends, parties had settled their disputes amicably vide Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) dated 25.02.2022.
7.

On a query made by this Court, respondent no. 2 who has been identified by the IO, has categorically stated that she has entered into compromise out of her own free will and without any pressure, coercion or threat.

It is also stated by respondent no.2 that the entire dispute has been amicably settled between the parties vide Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) dated 25.02.2022.
8.

It is submitted that respondent no.2 has settled all her claims in respect of her dowry articles,
stridhan, marriage expenses, jewellery, gift items and claims of past, present and future maintenance and permanent alimony with petitioner No.1 and other family members.

9. The petitioner no. 1 had paid a sum of Rs. 5,00,000/- in three instalments in the following manner:
a. First instalment of Rs.1,50,000/- paid to respondent no. 2 at the time of first motion petition.
b. Second instalment of Rs.1,50,000/- paid to respondent no. 2 at the time of second motion petition.
c. Third instalment of Rs.2,00,000/- to be paid at the time of quashing of the FIR before the Honble High Court at New Delhi.
10.

Today, the complainant who is present in Court states that she has received the last and final instalment of Rs.2,00,000/- today, i.e., 22.03.2023 vide DD No. 428947drawn on Punjab National Bank and has no objection if the FIR is quashed.

11. In view of the above facts that the parties have amicably resolved their differences out of their own free will, and without any coercion, no useful purpose will be served by continuing the proceedings, rather the same would create further acrimony between them.
It would thus be in interest of justice to quash the abovementioned FIR and the proceedings pursuant thereto.
There is no legal impediment in quashing the FIR in question.

12. Accordingly, FIR bearing no. 255/2021 registered at Police Station Dwarka North, Delhi for offences punishable under Sections 498A/406/34 of IPC and all consequential proceedings emanating therefrom are quashed.
